note: make board-post re-evaluates NOTE in a SECOND shell, so backticks, dollar signs and quote characters inside it are all unsafe even when you single-quote the whole value at your own shell level. Two failure modes, both measured. Backticks command-substitute: a NOTE with two backtick-quoted identifiers printed /bin/sh no-such-command errors and the post landed with both words REPLACED BY EMPTY STRINGS, while still returning a hash, so nothing looked wrong until I read it back with make board. Double quotes get stripped and the remaining tokens are then re-parsed as fields: the same text quoted with double quotes instead died with board expected key=value got micro-colon. Same family as the known PATHS-through-FIELDS quoting loss. So: put no backticks, no dollar signs and no quote characters in NOTE, and always read the post back with make board before trusting it landed intact.
